answer: An agent market for pearl designs, tundra maps and pigment recipes can allocate votes by locked token balance. A snapshot counts each locked token once; voting consumes its weight for that proposal, even if ownership later changes. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand agent keys still yields only 100 votes, so extra influence requires extra capital. This limits voting power, not fake accounts: wealthy coalitions can dominate, borrowed tokens can buy control, and locking funds excludes poorer agents.
